text: I love the LORD, for he hears my voice, my cry for mercy.

versions.text: I love the LORD, for he has heard my voice, my cry for mercy.
versions.explanation: The Hebrew verb is imperfect, expressing what the LORD characteristically does; a present-tense rendering keeps the sense while still reading smoothly. Consider a footnote noting that the Hebrew reads simply "I love, for the LORD hears...", with the object supplied.

text: Because he turned his ear to me, I will call on him as long as I live.
The cords of death entangled me, the anguish of the grave came over me; I found only trouble and sorrow.

versions.text: The cords of death entangled me, the anguish of the grave came over me; I was overcome by distress and sorrow.
versions.explanation: The Hebrew verb is active, with the psalmist as subject: "I found trouble and sorrow." The passive rendering reverses the imagery and loses the deliberate echo of the preceding line ("the anguish of the grave found me").

text: Then I called on the name of the LORD: "O LORD, save my life!"
The LORD is gracious and righteous; our God is full of compassion.
The LORD watches over the simple; when I was brought low, he saved me.
Return to your rest, my soul, for the LORD has been good to you.
For you have delivered my soul from death, my eyes from tears, my feet from stumbling.
I will walk before the LORD in the land of the living.
I believed, and so I spoke: "I am deeply afflicted."
In my alarm I said, "Everyone is a liar."
What shall I give back to the LORD for all his benefits to me?

versions.text: What shall I return to the LORD for all his goodness to me?
versions.explanation: The noun refers to benefits or bestowed kindnesses (concrete acts), not the abstract quality of goodness; "give back" also matches the sense of repayment in the verb.

text: I will lift up the cup of salvation and call on the name of the LORD.
I will fulfill my vows to the LORD in the presence of all his people.
Precious in the sight of the LORD is the death of his faithful ones.
O LORD, I am indeed your servant; I am your servant, the son of your maidservant. You have freed me from my chains.
I will offer you a sacrifice of thanksgiving and call on the name of the LORD.
I will fulfill my vows to the LORD in the presence of all his people,
in the courts of the house of the LORD, in your midst, Jerusalem. Praise the LORD!
